text:
Sam W: Heads-up: we have a regression on SM90 for the attention path — 7B streaming tail latency +18% vs SM80 in the nightly comparison.
Anya R: ugh. Where does it show up (kv hot path, prefix caching, batching)?
Sam W: Mostly during long-seq streaming with kv cache warm. Batching heuristics look normal. Repro: `./bench --model redwood-7b --seq 2048 --batch 4 --stream` on dedicated-pool-sm90.
Liam C: I did a quick `nsys`/`nvprof` run — looks like we fall back to a non-fused attention kernel around iteration 120. There's a series of memcpys right before attention.
Sam W: pasted the grep: ```
[ 120 ] choose_kernel: arch=sm_90 dtype=fp16 seq=2048 kv_paged=true -> selected=flash_paged_unfused
[ 121 ] runtime_check: failed warp_align -> fallback to generic_fused
```
Jorge M: Interesting — our kernel selection table has a rule that treats SM90 as having different warp alignment guarantees. Might be a conservative path introduced for Triton-compiled kernels.
Anya R: Are we comparing Triton vs hand-written CUDA? Which implementation regressed? Could be Triton-generated kernels with newer CUDA 12 optimizer changes.
Liam C: I recompiled the CUDA kernels with nvcc 12.2 and also ran the Triton build — the Triton variant shows higher L2 traffic for the paged variant on H100. nvprof shows increased `l2_hit` misses when using the paged/prefix kv layout.
Sam W: Perf numbers from the run: `SM80 (A100) fused-flash: p95=42ms`, `SM90 (H100) selected=flash_paged_unfused: p95=50ms`. CPU-side overhead for kernel selection ~0.6ms but memcopy spikes add ~6-7ms.
eng-bot: :rotating_light: alert perf-regression: attention-kernel-selection flagged by nightly-ci at 2026-03-12T03:12Z
Anya R: Hypothesis: heuristics pick paged variant for memory-savings but runtime path does extra copy to ensure 128B alignment on SM90, because of changed `ldmatrix` semantics or changes in preferred vector loads.
Jorge M: Yep. There's an alignment probe in the Triton wrapper: `if ((addr & 0x7f) != 0) memcpy_to_aligned_buffer()` — that code was added to handle older banks but may be unnecessary on H100.
Liam C: I tried forcing `select_kernel=force_flash_fused` at runtime; latency returns to SM80-levels on SM90. So kernel correctness is fine; selection + prep overhead is the issue.
Sam W: Nice find. So two levers: 1) tweak selection heuristics to prefer fused for certain seq/batch combos on SM90, 2) remove conservative alignment-copy on H100 after validating loads.
infra-sre: I can repro on staging H100 nodes. Happy to give a pinned machine for debugging. Also we should add a system test that runs `--seq 2048 --batch 4` across archs.
Anya R: Action items: (a) Liam/Jorge look into disabling the alignment memcpy when arch==sm_90 and validate correctness across sequence lengths (b) Sam to add arch-aware perf test in nightly CI (c) update selection table and add telemetry to capture when fallback happens.
Liam C: I'll open a draft PR with the memcpy gate + micro-bench results and post numbers here.
Jorge M: I'll update the kernel-selection rules and add a small micro-benchmark that compares fused vs paged for seq in [512,1024,2048].
Sam W: Thanks — please @mention me in both PRs. If we can get a fix today we can roll to a canary dedicated pool tomorrow.
eng-bot: deploy-plan created: attention-kernel-hotfix -> canary -> global (owner: Liam C)
Anya R: :thumbsup:
